corpus_note: SYNTHETIC corpus (scripts/make_synthetic.py, seeded) padded with the real parsed candidates. Used only to characterise retrieval behaviour vs corpus size — never for accuracy.

migration_triggers.action: move to an ANN index (FAISS IVF-PQ or HNSW), accepting ~1-2% recall loss
migration_triggers.why_not_now: at 500 candidates the exhaustive scan is sub-millisecond; an approximate index would trade accuracy for latency we do not need

migration_triggers.action: move to Qdrant or pgvector for transactional upserts and metadata filters
migration_triggers.why_not_now: single-process batch ingestion has no write contention

migration_triggers.symptom: index no longer fits in a single dyno's RAM
migration_triggers.action: shard by region or tenant; move to a managed store (Pinecone / OpenSearch)
migration_triggers.why_not_now: 500 candidates x ~6 chunks x 384 dims x 4 bytes is under 5 MB

migration_triggers.action: Postgres + pgvector with row-level security; per-tenant index namespaces
migration_triggers.why_not_now: single BD team, single trust boundary

migration_triggers.action: async task queue (Celery/SQS), object storage for documents, idempotent jobs keyed on file SHA-256, incremental index updates
migration_triggers.why_not_now: the pipeline already memoises on inputs_hash and threads across documents; at 10-500 documents a batch run is seconds

migration_triggers.action: incremental add/remove on the live index plus a background compaction
migration_triggers.why_not_now: full rebuild at 500 candidates takes under two seconds
